intended_object: For a Galois extension L/M of finite separable extensions of K(X), two places of L above the infinite place of K(X) are Galois-conjugate if some σ ∈ Gal(L/M) maps one to the other (σ(𝔓) = 𝔔). Inferred from the docstring, the name and the subsequent theorem exists_gal_smul_infinityPlace_asIdeal_of_same_under.
explanation: FiniteExtensionInfinityPlace K L is the set of primes over the maximal ideal of the valuation ring at ∞, taken in the integral closure of that ring in L. These are the places of L above ∞. infinityIntegralClosureGalAction restricts the Gal(L/M)-action on L to that integral closure, via Mathlib's IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction. The pointwise action on ideals then gives g • P.1 = σ(𝔓). So `∃ g, Q.1 = g • P.1` is exactly the standard conjugacy relation. Every place of L above ∞ lies over some place of M above ∞, so letting P and Q range over all places of L above ∞ is correct. The relation is specific to the library's encoding of the places at infinity over K(X). It is a thin predicate on that type, not a narrowed copy of a general Mathlib construction, so it is not too narrow.
